title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 117
paragraphs: When autumn came and the siege still went on, the Athenians became vexed at being absent from their own land and at the same time unable to conquer the fortress, and they begged their commanders to lead them home. But these said they would not do so until either they had taken the town or the public authority of the Athenians sent for them home. So they endured their present state.
